title: Common Fractions: Describing, Comparing, Adding and Equivalent Fractions
seo_title: Grade 4 Common Fractions Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Count forwards and backwards in fractions; compare and order common fractions with different denominators (halves, thirds, quarters, fifths, sixths, sevenths, eighths); describe and compare common fractions in diagram form; add common fractions with the same denominators; recognise, describe and use the equivalence of division and fractions; recognise and use equivalent forms of common fractions; solve problems involving fractions of whole numbers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 4 common fractions worksheets: fractions in diagrams, comparing and ordering, equivalent fractions, adding fractions and fractions of whole numbers. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Same numerator: smaller denominator, bigger fraction.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A common fraction has a numerator and a denominator: 35 means 3 of 5 equal parts.
  • With the same numerator, the smaller denominator is the bigger fraction: 13 > 16.
  • Equivalent fractions name the same amount: 12 = 24 = 48.
  • Add fractions with the same denominator: add the numerators, keep the denominator.
  • 34 of 20: 20 ÷ 4 = 5, 5 × 3 = 15.

Examples

Example

27 + 37

add the numerators: 2 + 3

Answer: 57

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Bigger denominator, bigger fractionEighths are smaller than quarters.
Adding denominatorsKeep the denominator.
Fraction of a numberDivide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 4 say about fractions?
faq.a: Count, compare and order common fractions (halves to eighths), describe and represent them in diagrams, add common fractions with the same denominators, recognise equivalent fractions, and find fractions of whole numbers.

items.q: What fraction of the shape is shaded?
items.e: The whole has 2 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 2. 1 part is shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 1. The answer is 12.

items.q: What fraction of the shape is shaded?
items.e: The whole has 4 equal parts, so the denominator (bottom number) is 4. 1 part is shaded, so the numerator (top number) is 1. The answer is 14.

items.q: What fraction of the shape is shaded?

items.q: What fraction of the shape is not shaded?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts. 1 is shaded, so 4 − 1 = 3 parts are not shaded. The answer is 34.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 12 is shaded. How many eighths are equal to 12?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 12 lines up with 4 eighths, because each half is the same as 4 eighths. So 12 = 48.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 34 is shaded. How many eighths are equal to 34?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 34 lines up with 6 eighths, because each quarter is the same as 2 eighths. So 34 = 68.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 23 is shaded. How many sixths are equal to 23?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 23 lines up with 4 sixths, because each third is the same as 2 sixths. So 23 = 46.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 15 is shaded. How many tenths are equal to 15?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. 15 lines up with 2 tenths, because each fifth is the same as 2 tenths. So 15 = 210.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Compare the fractions.
c: 13 = 16
13 > 16
13 < 16
items.e: Both are unit fractions. The whole is split into 3 parts or into 6 parts. More parts means smaller parts, so 13 > 16.

items.q: Compare the fractions. Choose <, > or =.
c: 18 > 14
18 = 14
18 < 14
items.e: Both are unit fractions. The whole is split into 8 parts or into 4 parts. More parts means smaller parts, so 18 < 14.

items.q: Which fraction is the smallest?
items.e: All are unit fractions. The biggest denominator means the smallest parts, so 18 is the smallest.

items.q: Which fraction is the greatest?
items.e: The denominators are the same, so the parts are the same size. The biggest numerator wins: 56.

items.q: Put the fractions in order, smallest first.
c: 14, 18, 12
18, 12, 14
12, 14, 18
18, 14, 12
items.e: For unit fractions, a bigger denominator means a smaller part. 18 is the smallest and 12 is the greatest.

items.q: Put the fractions in order, greatest first.
c: 67, 47, 17
67, 17, 47
47, 67, 17
17, 47, 67
items.e: The denominators are the same, so order the numerators: 6, 4, 1. Greatest first: 67, 47, 17.

items.q: A bar of chocolate has 5 equal pieces. Pieter eats 2 pieces. What fraction of the bar is left?
items.e: 5 − 2 = 3 pieces are left out of 5 equal pieces. The answer is 35.

items.q: There are 30 children in a Grade 3 class. 13 of them have school dinners. How many children have school dinners?
items.e: Share 30 into 3 equal groups: 30 ÷ 3 = 10 children. One group is 13.

items.q: Busisiwe has 20 sweets. 34 of them are red. How many red sweets are there?
items.e: First find 14: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. You need 3 groups, not 1: 5 × 3 = 15 sweets.

items.q: There are 24 learners in a class. 38 of them go to soccer club. How many learners go to soccer club?
items.e: First find 18: 24 ÷ 8 = 3. You need 3 groups, not 1: 3 × 3 = 9 learners.

items.q: Ravi eats 14 of a pizza. Kgomotso eats 16 of a pizza of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: A pizza cut into 4 has bigger slices than a pizza cut into 6. 14 > 16, so Ravi eats more.

items.q: A cake is cut into 8 equal pieces. Siyabonga eats 28 of it. Sipho eats 58 of it. Who eats less?
items.e: The pieces are the same size (eighths). 2 pieces is less than 5 pieces, so Siyabonga eats less.

items.q: Priya eats 12 of a sandwich. Ayanda eats 24 of a sandwich of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: 12 = 24. Ayanda has more pieces, but they are smaller. They eat the same amount.

items.q: Musa cuts a cake into 4 pieces. The pieces are different sizes. He says each piece is 14 of the cake. Is he right?
c: Yes, each piece is one part
No, the pieces are not equal
No, it should be 13
items.e: Quarters must be 4 equal parts. The pieces are different sizes, so they are not quarters.

items.q: There are 32 learners in a Grade 4 class. 38 of them have school dinners. How many learners have school dinners?
items.e: First find 18: 32 ÷ 8 = 4 learners. Then multiply by the numerator: 4 learners × 3 = 12 learners.

items.q: Busisiwe has a ribbon 60 cm long. She uses 34 of it to make a bow. How long is the piece for the bow?
items.e: First find 14: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 cm. Then multiply by the numerator: 15 cm × 3 = 45 cm.

items.q: Precious practises the piano for 34 of an hour. How many minutes is that?
items.e: There are 60 minutes in an hour (not 100). 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so 14 of an hour is 15 minutes. 15 × 3 = 45 minutes.

items.q: A book has 48 pages. Mpho has read 56 of it. How many pages does he have left to read?
items.e: 56 of 48: 48 ÷ 6 = 8, so 56 is 8 × 5 = 40 pages read. 48 − 40 = 8 pages left. (Quicker: 16 is left, and 16 of 48 is 8.)

items.q: Megan has a bag of 24 sweets. 13 of them are red. How many red sweets are there?
items.e: To find 13, divide by the denominator: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 sweets.

items.q: Naledi eats 24 of a chocolate bar. Neo eats 48 of a bar of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and denominator of 24 by 2: 24 = 48. Neo eats more pieces, but they are smaller, so they eat the same amount.

items.q: Vusi eats 34 of a pizza. Ethan eats 58 of a pizza of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: Change 34 to eighths: 34 = 68. 68 is more than 58, so Vusi eats more. A bigger denominator means smaller pieces.

items.q: There are 25 learners in a class. 35 of them walk to school. How many learners walk to school?
items.e: First find 15: 25 ÷ 5 = 5 learners. Then multiply by the numerator: 5 learners × 3 = 15 learners.

items.q: A cake is cut into 12 equal pieces. Kyle’s family eats 23 of the cake. How many pieces do they eat?
items.e: First find 13: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 pieces. Then multiply by the numerator: 4 pieces × 2 = 8 pieces.
